title: How effective are VLMs in assisting humans in inferring the quality of mental models from Multimodal short answers?
abstract: arXiv:2603.00056v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: STEM Mental models can play a critical role in assessing students' conceptual understanding of a topic. They not only offer insights into what students know but also into how effectively they can apply, relate to, and integrate concepts across various contexts. Thus, students' responses are critical markers of the quality of their understanding and not entities that should be merely graded. However, inferring these mental models from student answers is challenging as it requires deep reasoning skills. We propose MMGrader, an approach that infers the quality of students' mental models from their multimodal responses using concept graphs as an analytical framework. translated_title: 多模态短答案中，视觉语言模型在辅助人类推断心理模型质量方面的效果如何？
translated_abstract: 摘要：STEM领域的心理模型在评估学生对某一主题的概念理解中扮演着关键角色。它们不仅能揭示学生已知的内容，还能展示他们如何有效地应用、联系和整合不同情境下的概念。因此，学生的回答是理解质量的重要标志，而不仅仅是需要评分的对象。然而，从学生答案中推断这些心理模型具有挑战性，因为这需要深度推理能力。我们提出了MMGrader方法，该方法利用概念图作为分析框架，从学生的多模态回答中推断其心理模型的质量。在我们对9个公开可用模型的评估中，我们发现表现最佳的模型仍未能达到人类水平的表现。这是因为它们仅实现了约40%的准确率，预测误差为1.1个单位，且评分分布与人类评分存在显著偏差。
tldr: 本文提出MMGrader方法，利用概念图分析框架从多模态学生答案中推断心理模型质量，但评估显示最佳视觉语言模型准确率仅约40%，远未达到人类水平。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes MMGrader, which uses concept graphs to infer mental model quality from multimodal student answers, but evaluation shows that the best VLMs achieve only ~40% accuracy, falling short of human-level performance.
